statistics.label: UK Google searches ending without a click
statistics.statement: 69.5% of UK browser-based Google searches ended without a click in SparkToro's analysis of Similarweb data.
statistics.period: January–April 2026 in the shared method; UK period not separately confirmed
statistics.sample: Similarweb UK desktop and mobile-web panel; panel size not disclosed.
statistics.caveat: Excludes the Google mobile app. The shared method labels its period US. Zero-click activity does not establish satisfaction or isolate AI Overview effects.

statistics.label: Open-web clicks per 1,000 UK Google searches
statistics.statement: SparkToro estimated 232 clicks to the open web per 1,000 UK Google searches, including both organic and paid results.
statistics.period: January–April 2026 in the shared method; UK period not separately confirmed
statistics.caveat: This is not 232 organic visits. Multiple-result clicks may be undercounted. Alphabet-owned destinations are excluded from the open-web measure.

statistics.label: Google's share of UK search referrals
statistics.statement: Google generated 91.75% of UK search-engine referrals in Statcounter's August 2026 all-platform sample.
statistics.sample: Search-referred page views on sites with Statcounter measurement.
statistics.caveat: Measures clicked referrals, not searches or people. Zero-click activity is absent. August data remain within Statcounter's 45-day revision window.

statistics.label: Bing's share of UK desktop search referrals
statistics.statement: Bing generated 10.38% of UK desktop search-engine referrals in Statcounter's August 2026 sample.
statistics.sample: Search-referred desktop page views on Statcounter-network sites.
statistics.caveat: Publisher mix affects the sample. This is a device-specific referral share, not the share of UK adults using Bing. Recent data can be revised.

statistics.label: Bing's share of UK mobile search referrals
statistics.statement: Bing generated 0.48% of UK mobile search-engine referrals in Statcounter's August 2026 sample.
statistics.sample: Search-referred mobile page views on Statcounter-network sites.
statistics.caveat: Compare with the desktop figure only as referral shares. These values do not reveal the device split of all UK searches. Recent data can be revised.

statistics.label: Google's share of UK traditional search queries
statistics.statement: Google handled more than 90% of UK traditional general-search queries throughout January 2018 to June 2025, according to the CMA.
statistics.sample: CMA analysis of traditional general-search providers' query data.
statistics.caveat: Exact shares are confidential. This historical query measure is distinct from Statcounter referral shares and does not establish a September 2026 share.

statistics.label: UK search advertising expenditure
statistics.statement: UK search advertising expenditure reached £17.9bn in 2025, representing 44% of digital ad spend in IAB UK's study.
statistics.sample: IAB UK / Oliver Wyman revenue submissions, public figures and market modelling.
statistics.caveat: Paid search expenditure is not SEO agency revenue. The methodology changed in 2025; use the restated prior-year series for growth comparisons.

statistics.label: UK online adults who used search engines
statistics.statement: 96% of UK online adults reported using a search engine in the previous year in Ofcom's autumn 2025 survey.
statistics.sample: UK online adults aged 16+; 7,029 online respondents in the wider survey.
statistics.caveat: Self-reported annual use measures reach, not frequency or query volume. Survey changes limit year-on-year comparisons.

statistics.label: Search users selecting only the paid-placement explanation
statistics.statement: 52% of UK search-engine users selected only the correct paid-placement explanation in Ofcom's Google results test.
statistics.sample: 6,731 search-engine users aged 16+; a walking-boots search example.
statistics.caveat: 66% selected the paid-placement answer at all; 52% selected only that answer. This prompted test measures ad recognition, not organic CTR.

statistics.label: UK adults reporting AI-tool use
statistics.statement: 54% of UK adults reported using AI tools in Ofcom's autumn 2025 survey.
statistics.sample: 3,768 UK adults aged 16+ in survey Module 1.
statistics.caveat: Includes uses beyond search. Self-reported AI adoption is not an AI-search market share.

statistics.label: UK online adults reading AI search summaries
statistics.statement: 75% of UK online adults said they read AI-generated search summaries at least sometimes in Ofcom's autumn 2025 survey.
statistics.sample: 3,515 online adults aged 16+ in Module 1; prompted with a summary example.
statistics.caveat: Reported reading is not the frequency of summaries appearing, a citation rate or a measure of resulting clicks.

statistics.label: Conventional-result clicks with and without AI summaries
statistics.statement: Pew observed conventional-result clicks after 8% of US Google visits with an AI summary versus 15% without one.
statistics.caveat: Observational groups had different queries. Results were captured after the original searches. The comparison does not isolate a causal AI-summary effect.

statistics.label: AI-summary visits producing a source-link click
statistics.statement: Only 1% of visits to Google results with an AI summary produced a click on a cited summary link in Pew's US sample.
statistics.sample: 900 US adults; 12,593 observed searches with an AI summary.
statistics.caveat: Pew matched the next visited URL against the first three summary sources. A URL appearing in both places was counted as an AI-summary click.

statistics.label: Local searchers considering three or fewer businesses
statistics.statement: 72% of BrightLocal's active US local-searcher panel considered three or fewer businesses before choosing.
statistics.sample: 1,227 US consumers who searched online for a local business within three months.
statistics.caveat: Self-reported behaviour from a screened vendor survey. It is neither UK consumer behaviour nor observed Local Pack click-through rate.

statistics.label: CTR in the portfolio's rounded position-one bucket
statistics.statement: The rounded position-one bucket in Sunny Patel's 53-site portfolio study recorded 43 clicks from 721 impressions: 5.96% CTR.
statistics.sample: Five query rows in this bucket; 2,615 qualifying rows across the full study.
statistics.caveat: Small convenience sample. The published extraction script has no country filter or explicit brand exclusion. These are period-average position buckets, not fixed rankings or a UK benchmark.

statistics.label: Sample clicks from rounded position buckets 1–10
statistics.statement: Rounded position buckets 1–10 produced 1,448 of 1,667 clicks in Sunny Patel's portfolio dataset, or 86.9%.
statistics.sample: 53 managed sites; query rows with at least 50 impressions; bucketed GSC aggregates.
statistics.caveat: Calculated from the published aggregates. API extraction caps each property at 5,000 rows. Position buckets do not prove that moving a query causes the same gain.

statistics.label: Identified AI referral sessions across 12 sites
statistics.statement: Sunny Patel's published 12-site portfolio study reports 4,717 AI referral sessions from 28 May to 26 August 2026.
statistics.sample: GA4 session-source matching on the same 12 selected portfolio sites.
statistics.caveat: Sites were selected for high AI traffic. No country restriction or all-traffic denominator is supplied. Referral sessions do not measure citations, people or incremental sales.

statistics.label: ChatGPT's share of identified portfolio AI sessions
statistics.statement: ChatGPT and the grouped OpenAI source accounted for 4,250 of the study's 4,717 identified AI referral sessions, or 90.1%.
statistics.caveat: A share of identified AI referrals in this selected portfolio, not AI market share. Source attribution can miss untagged visits. Published totals are not an independent analytics audit.

zeroClickChart.period: Published 16 June 2026; shared method states January–April 2026 but labels that line US
